subject: MSA / Order Form: maintenance window tie-out & credit matrix
messages:
From: Helios Platform Ops <ops@helios.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@helios.io>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form: maintenance blackout & credit thresholds

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are the initial redlines from our ops and procurement teams (Helios_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf). A couple of items they asked us to confirm before routing to legal:

- Proposed maintenance blackout: weekly planned maintenance window (Sun 02:00-04:00 PT) — Helios would like this excluded from uptime calculations.
- Emergency patching: 4-hour emergency patch slots for critical CVEs; Helios wants no credits for these as long as notice is provided within 24 hours.
- Credit thresholds: our team is proposing a stepped credit matrix starting at 99.90 -> 99.99 with quarterly caps.

Can Redwood confirm whether the blackout exclusion and emergency-patch carveout align with your standard order form practice, and whether you can accept the credit caps in the attached spreadsheet?

We want to get this into procurement by next Tuesday — can you loop legal/ops on your side?

Thanks,
Sam Park
Helios Platform Ops


From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Helios Platform Ops <ops@helios.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: maintenance blackout & credit thresholds

Sam —

Appreciate the redlines. Quick take from Redwood:

1) Maintenance blackout: we can mark the weekly 02:00-04:00 PT window as a planned maintenance exclusion, but we need to preserve a maximum of 8 planned maintenance hours per calendar month (so customers can’t schedule unlimited weekly exclusions). Suggest language: "Planned maintenance (up to 8 hours/month) scheduled in the agreed maintenance window shall be excluded from uptime calculations if notice is provided 72 hours in advance."

2) Emergency patching: we are OK with a short emergency patch carveout but need it scoped. Proposed: emergency patch windows up to 4 hours are excluded only for P0 security patches where mitigation requires immediate restart and notice to customer is provided as soon as feasible and no later than 24 hours after action. Otherwise, incidents count against uptime.

3) Credit matrix & caps: attached is a suggested matrix (redline-summary.xlsx and proposed-credit-matrix.png). We propose starting credits at 99.95 as the first credit tier (rather than 99.90) given our multi-region failover. We can accept a quarterly cap equal to 3 months of monthly average revenue for the contracted services (order form line items) — but we prefer rolling caps to be limited to one invoice cycle if procurement requires lower exposure.

Next steps: Markus and Laura from Legal/Revenue Ops are CC’d — can you confirm Helios’s business prefers the 8-hours/month cap and 99.95 starting tier? If yes, we’ll return a clean counter with tracked changes and a DocuSign route for signatures. If procurement needs lower credit caps, we’ll need to put that on the commercial escalation path.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-summary.xlsx (summary of proposed credit tiers), proposed-credit-matrix.png


From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Helios Platform Ops <ops@helios.io>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: maintenance blackout & credit thresholds

Irene / Sam —

Two small legal/ops nits from our side that would smooth routing:

- Uptime baseline: confirm whether Helios requires regional or global availability measuring. We prefer global threshold for the service lines in this deal; if Helios insists on regional reporting, credits must be recalculated by region.
- Credit escalation cap: agree to the quarterly cap but request an absolute per-incident cap of 50% of the monthly fee for the affected service line to avoid outsized one-off liabilities.

If Helios is okay with global baseline and the per-incident cap, Laura will prep final redlines and I’ll approve for signature routing.

Markus Klein
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Helios Procurement <procurement@helios.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@helios.io>, Helios Platform Ops <ops@helios.io>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: maintenance blackout & credit thresholds

Hi Irene / Markus —

Thanks — Helios is comfortable moving forward on the following:

- Accepts the 8 hours/month planned maintenance cap for the agreed weekly window.
- Emergency patch carveout as scoped (P0 security only) is acceptable.
- Will accept a starting credit tier at 99.95 provided the per-incident cap is 50% monthly fee (Helios requests a maximum per-incident credit cap at 100% monthly fee — we will accept Redwood’s 50% proposal).
- Helios prefers regional reporting for high-availability services; however for this order form they are willing to accept global baseline for now and will request regional metrics as an addendum in 2027 Q1.

Please send the final redline and DocuSign routing. We will aim to complete signatures by EOD Thursday after reviewing the final counters.

Procurement Team
Helios

Forwarded attachment: DocuSign envelope (EMX-abcdef123456)
